subject: SignalStack integration: low-latency trace export & SLA runbook
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@signalstack.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: SignalStack Partnerships <partners@signalstack.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SignalStack <> Redwood: low-latency trace export integration

Hi Karthik —

Really enjoyed the demo last week. SignalStack would like to move forward with a lightweight integration that streams sampled OTLP traces from Redwood into our ingestion pipeline with a hard target: p95 end-to-end delivery under 250ms for regional traffic, and clear fallback behavior into a batched S3 export if the fast path degrades.

We put together an initial SLA draft and a short tech runbook (attached) that outlines the handshake, batching fallbacks, and a recommended sampling configuration. High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood can add a streaming route with a guaranteed low-latency path for a labeled subset of customer traffic (we can coordinate sampling keys).
- Provide suggested RBAC and KMS patterns for the streaming route.
- Agree an ops runbook for incidents where p95 > 250ms (circuit breaker thresholds, alerting, and automatic fallback).

Can you point me to the right eng partners internally to iterate the runbook? If helpful, we can book a short working session next week (30 min).

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Partnerships, SignalStack
--

Hi Maya — thanks and glad to hear it went well.

High level: we can support a dedicated streaming route for sampled traces. A few quick questions before the working session so we come prepared:
1) Is the 250ms p95 target measured at the point of Redwood egress or end-to-end (customer SDK -> SignalStack UI)? We should be explicit because network hops and Partner ingestion can add variance.
2) Expected peak QPS for the fast path (sampled traces/sec) and burst profile — that determines pool sizing.
3) Do you expect encryption via customer-managed keys (KMS) or partner-managed?

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Ben (platform ops) and Laura (partner eng) to draft a short SLA + incident runbook.
- Can we do a 30-minute working session on Tue 2027-06-08 10:00 PT? If that works, please send a calendar invite and any network diagrams you want to share beforehand.

Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Forwarding SignalStack's ask — key points: p95 <= 250ms fast-path target, fallback to batched S3 export on degradation, and guidance on KMS/RBAC. Attached SLA draft from SignalStack.

Ben/Laura — can you review the runbook sections related to:
- Pool sizing and circuit-breaker defaults we should recommend (pool config + per-model tokenization costs not relevant here but note CPU/IO impact).
- Preferred TLS/KMS pattern if customer keys are requested (we should list recommended IAM policies).
- Ops play: what alerts (metric names + thresholds) we want to auto-trigger fallback and an SRE escalation path.

Connor — can you validate whether our continuous-batching runtime can export a sampled prefix stream with <5ms addl per-message overhead under normal load? If not, we need to set more conservative p95.

I added a placeholder Drive link where we'll keep the runbook notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedRunbook

Thanks — Karthik

Quick notes after skimming the draft SLA and runbook:
- Pool sizing: for an initial pilot with 5k sampled traces/sec peak we recommend 2 x medium GPU workers with a 30% headroom buffer and a short-lived burst pool for spikes. I'll paste config snippets below (also attached).
- Circuit breaker: fire when p95 send_latency > 320ms for 60s (then 10s backoff, escalate at 5 failures). This gives some breathing room vs their 250ms target and accounts for partner ingestion variance.
- Metrics: rtw.fastpath.send_latency.p95, rtw.fastpath.error_rate, rtw.fastpath.queue_depth. Alert if p95 > 320ms or error_rate > 0.5% sustained 2m.

Attaching: rtw_config_snippets.yaml (contains example pool settings + rolling config).

Ben
Platform Ops
